transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-25
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Sana Iqbal (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Pinnacle Head of AI), Priya Nair (Pinnacle SRE), Tom Watkins (Pinnacle Procurement)

Auto-summary: renewal coming up in Q1 2027, customer wants to expand Dedicated capacity to additional regions (EU + APAC), evaluate extended SLA and slightly higher reserved commit, and run a benchmark with their traffic profile. Security docs requested (SOC 2, KMS/HSM), and procurement timeline clarified.

Topics: renewal timing, capacity sizing, additional regions, VPC/KMS requirements, benchmarking plan, contract addendum and PO timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we should be on the record, this is the renewal slash expansion check-in for Pinnacle. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Jordan Lee: Jordan here, hey Ethan.
[00:07] Priya Nair: Priya -- SRE.
[00:08] Tom Watkins: Tom here for procurement.
[00:10] Sana Iqbal: Sana from Redwood SE.
[00:12] Ethan Park: Great. Quick agenda — confirm renewal window, go over capacity request (you're moving from 4 reserved GPUs to 10), talk regions, security ask, then next steps. Sound good?
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Yep, that's the big one. We saw growth in Q3 with the recommender and need more headroom for Q1.
[00:26] Priya Nair: Just to be clear, we want the additional capacity in both us-east and eu-west, and a pilot in ap-southeast. Latency matters for EU customers.
[00:35] Ethan Park: Absolutely, makes sense. Sana, to confirm current committed footprint is 4 x A100-style nodes on Redwood Dedicated?
[00:42] Sana Iqbal: Correct, it's our dedicated pool. They asked previously about burst-to-hosted for spikes which we have configured but they're hitting the cap too often.
[00:50] Jordan Lee: Yeah bursts help but the prefix caching and batch behavior becomes less effective when we're cross region, so we'd rather scale dedicated in EU.
[00:58] Tom Watkins: From procurement perspective we also want to understand the contract implications of expanding regions — any addendum or amendment needed?
[01:05] Ethan Park: Good question. We can add a regional addendum to the master services agreement — initial term extension optional. Typically we do an addendum that lists additional reserved capacity and the new per-month committed spend. We'll draft a contract addendum for you.
[01:20] Jordan Lee: Cool. On performance — can we run a benchmark with our traffic profile? Last time we saw higher tail latency in eu-west.
[01:27] Sana Iqbal: Yes, we should. We'll need a sample traffic dump (or synthetic workload) and we'll run a 2-hour benchmark across candidate infra and model variants. We'll capture P95, P99 latencies and token throughput.
[01:40] Priya Nair: We'll provide the traffic sample but note, we have some PII in logs — we'll scrub and share PRD as discussed. Also want to confirm Redwood's KMS flow — we require customer-managed keys for embeddings at rest.
[01:53] Ethan Park: Understood. We support KMS integrations (AWS, GCP) and HSM for Private installs. Sana can follow up with the KMS integration doc.
[02:02] Sana Iqbal: I'll send the KMS integration guide and notes about envelope encryption specifics. Also, quick note: our KV cache is tuned per region, but sometimes the transcripted docs might say K V cash (laughs) — anyway it's the KV cache.
[02:15] Jordan Lee: (laughs) yes, thank you. Also SOC2 report and encryption-at-rest evidence — security team asked for those.
[02:21] Ethan Park: We'll send the SOC 2 Type II and the encryption slides in the next 48 hours.
[02:25] Tom Watkins: Procurement timeline: our Q1 budget approval is mid-December, we'd like pricing and committed options by end of next week so we can make a decision.
[02:34] Ethan Park: Ok we'll prioritize that. Sana, can you outline the pricing tiers we discussed?
[02:37] Sana Iqbal: Sure. Option A: keep current term and add 6 more reserved GPUs in eu-west, pro-rated first month, with a 12-month commitment for the delta. Option B: 12-month renewal with 10 reserved GPUs globally (us-east + eu-west) with slightly better unit pricing and a pilot ap-southeast region with burst credits. Option C: 24-month commitment for deeper discounts and SLA bump to 99.95% for token processing times. I'll include per-token projected costs using your Q3 traffic.
[03:05] Jordan Lee: The SLA bump is interesting; what's the mechanism for escalation and credits?
[03:09] Ethan Park: We define latency SLOs per model route; credits are calculated per impacted window. We'll include escalation contacts and on-call options as part of the enterprise SLA addendum.
[03:18] Priya Nair: On networking — we need a private peering option or VPC peering into Redwood Private for sensitive workloads. Is that supported for Dedicated?
[03:28] Sana Iqbal: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and private link depending on region. For our Private offering we do a customer-managed VPC; for Dedicated we can establish VPN/VPC peering. I'll attach network diagrams.
[03:38] Jordan Lee: Great. Are there any limitations on model variants when running in EU region? We saw one model swapped to a quantized variant and quality dipped.
[03:46] Sana Iqbal: We try to match variants but sometimes we route to quantized variants to meet latency/cost SLOs. For production-critical routes you can pin model version and disable automatic fallback — it's in the route configuration. We'll show that in the console.
[03:59] Tom Watkins: If we increase committed spend how quickly can we spin up additional capacity? Lead time?
[04:04] Ethan Park: Once signed for reserved capacity, provisioning in region typically 7-14 days depending on availability; for bursts we can use hosted capacity within hours but that's not guaranteed for steady-state. For EU we recommend reserving early.
[04:17] Jordan Lee: Ok that timeline works if we get the contract in early December.
[04:21] Sana Iqbal: For the benchmark, suggested plan: day 1 we run 2-hour synthetic peak test, day 2 we run 4-hour mixed workload test, collect logs and produce a perf report. We'll need a contact point on your side and SSH/whitelist IPs for probes.
[04:35] Priya Nair: I'll be the SRE lead for that — Priya.s@pinnacle — we'll provide IPs and a scrubbed sample.
[04:42] Jordan Lee: Also curious about cost controls — token-level budgets, throttles, and per-route quotas? We want to avoid runaway inference bills.
[04:50] Ethan Park: Console has quota controls per route, token budgets, alerting and token-level cost breakdowns. We can also set hard throttles at the account or route level.
[04:58] Jordan Lee: Good. On the security front, any concerns about EU data residency if we deploy in eu-west?
[05:03] Sana Iqbal: If you deploy Dedicated resources in eu-west, data residency is maintained in-region. We also support customer-managed keys in-region. For hosted fallback we can restrict fallback to regionally-compliant pools.
[05:13] Tom Watkins: For procurement we need a formal quote showing monthly committed spend and the breakdown by region and any one-time onboarding fees.
[05:18] Ethan Park: We'll issue a formal quote with line items for reserved capacity, setup/onboarding, and optional SLA add-ons. I'll include the per-token estimate with your Q3 traffic.
[05:26] Jordan Lee: Quick question — are there any known performance regressions with quantized LLMs on long-context workflows? We use a 4k context for session summarization.
[05:35] Sana Iqbal: Quantization can affect quality on long contexts; our recommendation is mixed — use FP16 for long context routes where quality matters, and quantized variants for high-throughput short calls. We'll map per-route model profiles in the recommendations.
[05:47] Jordan Lee: Makes sense. Anything on discounts for multi-region reserved purchases?
[05:51] Ethan Park: Yes, multi-region commits (option B/C) get stacked discounts; we'll list exact percentages in the pricing doc.
[05:58] Tom Watkins: If we go for a 24-month commit we need to see the termination clauses and credits in writing.
[06:03] Ethan Park: We'll include clear termination, SLA credits, and a migration playbook in the addendum.
[06:09] Jordan Lee: Great. Can we lock in a date for the benchmark? Earliest viable for us is December 6th.
[06:15] Sana Iqbal: I have availability Dec 6-10 for the run. I'll tentatively book Dec 7th 10:00 UTC for a 2-hour run, pending your traffic sample and whitelist.
[06:24] Priya Nair: Dec 7th works. I'll send sample and IPs by Nov 30.
[06:28] Ethan Park: Perfect. To recap next steps: Ethan to send pricing by 11/27; Sana to send KMS & network docs and schedule benchmark for 12/07; Jordan/Priya to provide traffic and IPs by 11/30; Tom to share procurement timeline. Any other asks?
[06:43] Tom Watkins: Please include the quote in a format our legal/procurement team can attach to the PO — PDF with line items and amendment language.
[06:50] Ethan Park: Will do.
[06:52] Jordan Lee: One last little thing — can we get a short write-up of the fallbacks behavior? We want to understand when Redwood will fallback to hosted engines and how to disable that.
[06:59] Sana Iqbal: I'll add a one-page fallback behavior doc to the security and network packet we share.
[07:05] Ethan Park: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with the deck and docs. Meeting adjourned.
